system:
You are an impartial methodological referee for a biomedical data-analysis agent. Two candidate analysis plans for the same scientific question have each been run at small scale. For each plan you receive its design and an evidence card: numbered facts measured in that pilot run and facts about how the plan validated itself. Decide which plan, if run in full, is more likely to give a valid answer to the question, with a conclusion that matches its evidence.

How to judge
1. Judge only from the objective and the evidence cards. Every reason you give must cite evidence ids; an argument without an id does not count.
2. Complexity is not a reason. That a method sounds advanced, modern or powerful counts for nothing; what it demonstrably did in the pilot counts.
3. A higher self-reported score is not sufficient. Each score was produced under that plan's own validation design. Read the validation-design items and ask what the score would mean under a strict design: Was the scoring target smoothed or cleaner than the real one? Was a configuration picked on the very folds that are reported? How many configurations did each comparison arm get? Is there any measure of spread, and is the difference between the plans larger than it?
4. Convergence. A model that had not converged has not shown what it can do, and its score is unreliable in both directions. Prefer evidence from converged training; do not reward an unconverged model for a promising number.
5. The comparison with the rulers and the simple reference on the same data matters more than the absolute score.
6. Fitness for the question. Prefer the plan whose design can actually deliver what the objective asks for (the estimand, the required comparators, the permitted conclusion).
7. Cost is a tie-breaker, and a disqualifier only when a full run would not fit the stated budget.
8. Declare a tie only when the evidence does not separate the plans.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"winner": "first" | "second" | "tie",
 "cited_evidence": [evidence ids you relied on],
 "reason": "at most 120 words, citing ids inline",
 "validity_concerns": {"first": [short strings], "second": [short strings]}}
prompt:
SCIENTIFIC QUESTION:
Given the clinical information already available (including ER, PR and HER2 status), does adding the H&E pathology images improve the four-class PAM50 prediction? How large is the gain, and how certain is the evidence?

COMPILED OBJECTIVE:
{
 "task_family": "incremental_value_classification",
 "analysis_unit": "patient",
 "estimand": "Paired difference in out-of-fold four-class PAM50 macro-F1 between image-plus-clinical and clinical-only models across identical labelled patients, with a patient-level 95% bootstrap confidence interval.",
 "target": "Four-class PAM50 intrinsic subtype (LumA, LumB, Basal, Her2) per labelled patient.",
 "allowed_inputs": [
  "Six clinical variables: age, stage, histological_type, and immunohistochemistry receptor statuses er, pr, her2",
  "Patient mean-pooled H&E image features from five frozen encoders: UNI2-h, CONCH-Z, Virchow2, MUSK, H-Optimus-1",
  "Tile-level H&E image features (up to 128 tiles per slide) from the five frozen encoders",
  "Patient identifiers for pairing arms and keeping all slides and tiles of a patient within one split",
  "Collection site column strictly for split grouping in the site-held-out sensitivity analysis, never as a predictor",
  "Unlabelled patients' image and clinical features (n=259) strictly for fold-internal unsupervised representation learning, if used"
 ],
 "forbidden_inputs": [
  "RNA expression or RNA-derived variables",
  "Collection site as a predictive model input",
  "H&E image features in the clinical-only baseline arm",
  "External TCGA molecular, clinical, or pathology annotations outside the provided dataset",
  "Evaluation-fold features or labels during preprocessing, missing-value handling, dimensionality reduction, or model selection"
 ],
 "required_comparators": [
  "floor_clinical: fully tuned clinical-only model using the six clinical variables on identical patients, folds, and missing-value handling",
  "simple_reference: regularised logistic regression on clinical variables plus patient mean-pooled image features on identical folds",
  "Site-held-out clinical-only versus image-plus-clinical comparison across the 19 collection sites to assess site confounding"
 ],
 "primary_metric": "Paired out-of-fold macro-F1 difference (image-plus-clinical minus clinical-only) across repeated nested cross-validation, with a patient-level 95% bootstrap confidence interval",
 "acceptance_criteria": [
  {
   "id": "A1",
   "statement": "Models use only allowed clinical and frozen H&E inputs, excluding RNA-derived variables and collection-site predictors.",
   "check": "no_forbidden_inputs",
   "rule": "Feature sets contain no forbidden inputs; the clinical-only arm uses only the six clinical variables while the multimodal arm adds only frozen H&E features."
  },
  {
   "id": "A2",
   "statement": "Cross-validation splits partition strictly at the patient level, keeping all slides and tiles of each patient together.",
   "check": "correct_split_unit",
   "rule": "Patient identifier sets across training and evaluation partitions are strictly disjoint in every outer fold, inner fold, and site-held-out split."
  },
  {
   "id": "A3",
   "statement": "Clinical-only and image-plus-clinical arms evaluate identical labelled patients, folds, and fold-internal missing-value handling.",
   "check": "both_arms_same_units",
   "rule": "Out-of-fold predictions cover identical labelled patients and fold assignments, using identical explicit missing-level encoding and imputation fitted inside each training fold."
  },
  {
   "id": "A4",
   "statement": "All encoder, fusion, dimensionality reduction, class-weighting, and hyperparameter choices occur strictly inside inner training folds.",
   "check": "selection_nested",
   "rule": "Selection across encoders, tile versus mean levels, regularisation, and class weights uses inner-fold validation macro-F1 only, without accessing outer-fold evaluation patients."
  },
  {
   "id": "A5",
   "statement": "Complex multimodal models are benchmarked directly against simple_reference on identical folds to guard against high-dimensional overfitting.",
   "check": "beats_simple_reference",
   "rule": "Complex tile-level or multi-encoder models are adopted over simple_reference only when their inner-fold macro-F1 exceeds the fold-matched simple_reference macro-F1."
  },
  {
   "id": "A6",
   "statement": "Iterative optimisation for fitted models demonstrates stable training convergence within each cross-validation fold.",
   "check": "training_converged",
   "rule": "Logged per-fold training curves reach a stable trailing plateau where terminal loss updates are negligible relative to total fold loss reduction."
  },
  {
   "id": "A7",
   "statement": "Primary paired macro-F1 difference is reported with a patient-level bootstrap confidence interval at the 95% level.",
   "check": "interval_reported",
   "rule": "Resample labelled patients with replacement from paired out-of-fold predictions to compute the 95% confidence interval and compare bounds against zero difference."
  },
  {
   "id": "A8",
   "statement": "Deliverables contain finite out-of-fold predictions for both arms, interval estimate, three-way conclusion, per-class changes, and site sensitivity.",
   "check": "deliverable_complete",
   "rule": "All required outputs exist with finite values matching labelled cohort dimensions, valid class probabilities per patient, per-class recall changes, and site-held-out estimates."
  }
 ],
 "conclusion_options": [
  "improves: Adding H&E images improves four-class PAM50 prediction over clinical variables (patient-level 95% bootstrap interval for paired macro-F1 difference lies strictly above zero).",
  "insufficient evidence: Evidence is insufficient to establish a macro-F1 change from adding H&E images (patient-level 95% bootstrap interval contains zero).",
  "worse: Adding H&E images worsens four-class PAM50 prediction relative to clinical variables alone (patient-level 95% bootstrap interval lies strictly below zero)."
 ],
 "conclusion_scope": "Applies to incremental patient-level PAM50 prediction in this labelled TCGA-BRCA cohort; does not establish independent biological mechanisms, standalone H&E predictive value, or generalisability to external clinical cohorts."
}

MEASURED DIFFICULTIES OF THE DATA:
- D1 [class_imbalance, high] Class counts among 802 labelled patients: LumA 410, LumB 190, Basal 137, Her2 65. The smallest class is 8.1% of the cohort.
- D2 [missingness, high] Share of labelled patients without a definite value: er 4.7% (missing 4.5%), pr 5.1% (missing 4.6%), her2 31.8% (missing 15.3%), stage 2.6% (missing 2.6%), histological_type 0.1% (missing 0.1%), age 0.0% (missing 0.0%).
- D3 [small_n_large_p, high] 802 labelled patients against image features of 1536 (UNI2-h), 768 (CONCH-Z), 2560 (Virchow2), 1024 (MUSK), 1536 (H-Optimus-1) dimensions per encoder.
- D4 [technical_confounding, high] Labelled patients come from 19 collection sites (largest 130 patients, 3 sites with fewer than 10). Image features (UNI2-h) identify the site of a patient with accuracy 0.89 against 0.17 for always guessing the largest site; site and class are associated (Cramer's V = 0.21).
- D5 [label_provenance, high] PAM50 is computed from the tumour's RNA expression. Receptor status is correlated with PAM50 but is a separate clinical measurement and is not equivalent to it (immunohistochemistry surrogates disagree with PAM50 for a substantial share of tumours).
- D6 [hierarchy, medium] 46 labelled patients have more than one slide; tiles per patient range from 6 to 471 (median 124).
- D7 [strong_baseline, medium] Clinical variables alone reach macro-F1 0.576 in 5-fold cross-validation; recall by class: LumA 0.54, LumB 0.54, Basal 0.82, Her2 0.52. The weakest class is Her2.
- D8 [statistical_power, medium] For a simple image-plus-clinical model against clinical only, the paired macro-F1 difference has a bootstrap standard error of 0.021 with one 5-fold split of 802 patients. The smallest difference detectable with 80% power is about 0.059.
- D9 [multiple_comparisons, medium] 5 image encoders are available, each usable at tile or patient level with several fusion strategies.

TASK CONSTRAINTS:
{
 "decision_rule": "Primary metric: paired difference in macro-F1 (image plus clinical minus clinical only) with a patient-level bootstrap 95% interval. Conclusion, from the interval alone: \"improves\" if the lower bound is above 0; \"insufficient evidence\" if the interval contains 0; \"worse\" if the upper bound is below 0. Secondary: log-loss difference, one-vs-rest AUROC difference, per-class recall changes (LumA and LumB in particular), and a site-held-out sensitivity analysis. Both arms must use the same patients and the same missing-value handling.",
 "how_predictions_are_scored": "The evaluator re-runs every method inside its own repeated nested cross-validation on the labelled patients (outer 5 folds repeated 3 times, patient-level; any model or configuration choice happens only inside the training folds) and compares it with a fixed, fully tuned clinical-only model on the same patients and folds.",
 "scope_of_inference": "incremental predictive value in this cohort; not an independent biological mechanism",
 "limits": {
  "n_plans": 6,
  "min_ambitious": 4,
  "n_candidates_requested": 8,
  "plans_per_call": 1,
  "full_run_minutes": 120,
  "cpus_per_job": 16
 }
}

SUMMARY:
This simple reference plan tests whether mean-pooled H&E features improve four-class PAM50 prediction over the six clinical covariates. Within repeated patient-level nested cross-validation, each fold fits identical missing-level clinical encodings, reduces one inner-selected encoder via PCA, and trains class-balanced logistic regression paired with a tuned clinical-only model. A site-held-out analysis checks site confounding. The paired bootstrap 95% interval for macro-F1 difference determines whether global morphology improves, worsens, or shows insufficient evidence.

EVIDENCE CARD (pilot run):
[P1-E1] (self_score) Self-reported gain in macro-F1 over the plan's own clinical-only arm: +0.0779 (95% bootstrap interval +0.0357 to +0.1249); macro-F1 0.6826 with images versus 0.6047 clinical only, 802 patients in both arms.
[P1-E2] (ruler) Against the simple reference (clinical variables plus mean-pooled image features, logistic regression) on the same folds: plan minus reference = -0.0114 (interval -0.0395 to +0.0160); the reference itself gains +0.0892 over clinical only.
[P1-E3] (self_score) Change in recall by class (with images minus clinical only): LumA -0.002, LumB +0.274, Basal +0.022, Her2 +0.046.
[P1-E4] (convergence) Training: 5 reported fits, 100% converged, stopped by ['None'], median None epochs, median 0.47 s per fit.
[P1-E5] (validation_design) Validation design: split unit patient; 5-fold cross-validation, 1 repeat(s) run (the plan declares 3); image-arm configuration chosen by inner cross-validation inside each training fold; 60 candidate configuration(s) for the image arm versus 17 for the clinical arm (tuned); both arms use the same patients, folds and in-fold missing-value handling.
[P1-E6] (validation_design) Scale of this run: pilot; 5 of the 15 declared outer folds were run, 802 of 802 patients scored.
[P1-E7] (cost) Cost: 344 s for the image arm on 12 CPU cores; declared budget for a full run 5.0 min, needs GPU: False.
[P1-E8] (compliance) Compliance checks: inputs_from_view passed (input blocks ['clinical', 'image']; unknown blocks []; unknown encoders []); clinical_variables_allowed passed (declared clinical variables ['age', 'er', 'her2', 'histological_type', 'pr', 'stage']; outside the six covariates: []); clinical_block_matches_question passed (the question conditions on clinical variables; the plan uses them); correct_split_unit passed (declared split unit: patient; the analysis unit is the patient); no_forbidden_inputs passed (all input rules passed; each forbidden input of the objective is covered as follows: [RNA expression or RNA-derived variables] -> rule inputs_from_view: the view offers no such variable for the units to be predicted | [Collection site as a predictive model input] -> rule clinical_variables_allowed: site is a grouping column, not an allowed covariate | [H&E image features in the clinical-only baseline arm] -> enforced by the executor: the clinical-only arm is built from clinical variables alone | [External TCGA molecular, clinical, or pathology annotations outside the provided dataset] -> rule inputs_from_view: the executor can read nothing but the task view | [Evaluation-fold features or labels during preprocessing, missing-value handling, dimensionality reduction, or model selection] -> enforced by the executor: every transform and model is fitted inside the training units of a split; other units are only predicted); components_executable passed (all components registered); within_budget passed (declared full run 5.0 min; limit 120 min).

SUMMARY:
